options: Builds every selected model in the project, in dependency order
Only checks the connection, without building anything
Deletes all existing tables before doing anything else
Only runs tests, never builds models
questions.explain: dbt run builds every selected model, resolving ref() calls to determine the correct dependency order first.

questions.q: In the real dbt run output shown in this lesson, what does the line `Found 2 models, 4 tests, ... 0 sources` represent?
options: dbt's first pass — parsing files and resolving ref() calls, before anything has actually run
The final result of the run
A list of errors encountered
The number of rows written to the warehouse
questions.explain: That line is dbt's parse-and-resolve pass, counting what it found in the project before any model actually builds.

questions.q: What is the one line in the run output this lesson says you should always check first?
options: The final 'Done. PASS=... WARN=... ERROR=... SKIP=...' summary line
The first line of the terminal output
The dbt version number
The name of the target warehouse
questions.explain: The final Done. PASS/WARN/ERROR/SKIP line is the run-level tally that tells you, at a glance, whether everything succeeded.

questions.q: What happens to models downstream of a model that fails during a run?
options: They get SKIPped — dbt won't build them on top of data that just failed to build correctly
They run anyway, using whatever data is already there
dbt automatically fixes the failing model and continues
The entire warehouse connection is dropped
questions.explain: dbt marks downstream models as SKIP rather than building them against upstream data that failed, protecting the rest of the run.

questions.q: In the run output, what distinguishes a model that shows `[CREATE TABLE]` from one that shows `[CREATE VIEW]`?
options: Its materialization — how that specific model is configured to be built
Whether the model contains a JOIN
The number of columns it has
Whether it uses a ref() call or not
questions.explain: CREATE TABLE vs. CREATE VIEW reflects each model's materialization setting, covered in depth in Lesson 11.
